summary: Blueprint of Motivic and étale K-theory, Part II: fundamental lines and special-value factors. For K-theoretic motive data h^i(X)(j) over number fields (a smooth projective variety with a regular proper model, a Chow–Künneth projector, a twist and a coefficient algebra) it defines the Burns–Flach motivic factors H⁰_f, H¹_f from cycles, Adams eigenspaces and integral images of MotivicEtaleKTheory, with their weight vanishing, and computes them for Artin and elliptic motives (FL.1); builds the real Deligne complex, the Beilinson regulator sequence, the real exactness predicate, proves it for all Tate twists of Artin motives (Borel, Dirichlet) and for h¹(E)(1) (Néron–Tate), and constructs the real comparison of the fundamental line (FL.2); builds the p-adic realization maps into Bloch–Kato Selmer complexes, the realization predicate, proves it for Artin motives at every prime (Soulé, Kummer) and relates it to Sha for h¹(E)(1), computes the Selmer complexes of Artin motives and constructs the p-adic comparison with its Euler-factor normalization (FL.3); and states Kato's rational zeta element condition, proves its equivalence with the commutative Tamagawa obstruction of PeriodsAndSpecialValues, its lattice, place-set, duality and Selmer forms, the class number formula case and the cohomological Lichtenbaum form, and supplies the elliptic data used for BSD (FL.4).

nodes.title: K-theoretic motive datum
nodes.statement: A K-theoretic motive datum M = (K, X, 𝒳, π, i, j, A, φ) consists of: a number field K; a smooth projective K-scheme X of pure dimension d (not necessarily geometrically connected); a regular proper flat O_K-model 𝒳 of X, part of the data (for X = Spec F with F/K finite, 𝒳 = Spec O_F); an idempotent Chow correspondence π ∈ CH^d(X ×_K X) ⊗ Q whose Betti, de Rham and ℓ-adic realizations are concentrated in the single cohomological degree i (so that the Chow motive (X, π) is h^i of its realizations); a twist j ∈ ℤ; a finite-dimensional semisimple ℚ-algebra A and a ring homomorphism φ : A → π·(CH^d(X × X) ⊗ ℚ)·π into the endomorphisms of the Chow motive (X, π). Write M = h^i(X)(j) = (X, π, j), its weight w = i − 2j, and its dual datum M*(1) = (X, πᵗ, 2d − i, d + 1 − j) with A^op acting by transposed correspondences.
hypotheses: K is a number field and X is smooth projective of pure dimension d over K.
π is idempotent and its realizations are concentrated in degree i; for Artin motives (X = Spec F, i = 0) and elliptic curves (π¹ = Δ − e × E − E × e, i = 1) such projectors are explicit.
The model 𝒳 is regular, proper and flat over O_K and is recorded as data; no statement in this roadmap asserts independence of the model beyond the cases proved in FL.1/artin-motive-factors.
proofSteps: Use the Chow motives, Tate twists, transposition and duals of MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.1 (chow-motive, tate-twist, motives-rigid) to form (X, π, j) and its dual (X, πᵗ, d − j); twist the dual by one to get M*(1).
Read off the realizations from MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2 (betti-realization, de-rham-realization, etale-realization) and check that π cuts out degree i in each.
Record the model 𝒳 for the integral parts of FL.1/motivic-factor-spaces, as MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/integral-motivic-structures does.
acceptance: For X = Spec F, π = Δ, i = 0: the weight is −2j and the dual datum is (Spec F, Δ, 0, 1 − j).
For an elliptic curve E with π¹: the weight of h¹(E)(j) is 1 − 2j and the dual datum is h¹(E)(2 − j) after the Weil-pairing identification of FL.1/elliptic-motive-factors.

nodes.title: Motivic cohomology factors H⁰_f and H¹_f
nodes.statement: For a K-theoretic motive datum M = h^i(X)(j) define the finite-dimensional-by-hypothesis A-modules H⁰_f(K, M) and H¹_f(K, M) as follows. H⁰_f(K, M) = π_*((CH^j(X)/CH^j(X)_{hom∼0}) ⊗ ℚ) if i = 2j and 0 otherwise, homological equivalence being taken in Betti cohomology for the embeddings of K. H¹_f(K, M) = 0 if 2j − i − 1 < 0; = π_*(CH^j(X)_{hom∼0} ⊗ ℚ) if 2j − i − 1 = 0; and if 2j − i − 1 > 0 it is π_* of the image of the weight-j Adams eigenspace (K_{2j−i−1}(𝒳) ⊗ ℚ)^{(j)} → (K_{2j−i−1}(X) ⊗ ℚ)^{(j)}, that is, of the rational integral part im[H^{i+1}_M(𝒳, ℚ(j)) → H^{i+1}_M(X, ℚ(j))] of MotivicEtaleKTheory §12.3. The factors H⁰_f(K, M*(1)) and H¹_f(K, M*(1)) are those of the dual datum, and A acts through φ by functoriality of K-theory and Chow groups under correspondences.
hypotheses: The regular proper model 𝒳 is the one recorded in the datum.
Finite dimensionality of H¹_f is not asserted in general; it is a hypothesis wherever a determinant is taken, and a theorem in FL.1/artin-motive-factors and, for j = 1, FL.1/elliptic-motive-factors.
proofSteps: Take the Adams eigenspace and the integral image from MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/integral-motivic-structures and the rational weight decomposition of M.6/rational-weight-comparison; the higher Chow description H^{i+1}_M(X, ℚ(j)) = CH^j(X, 2j − i − 1)_ℚ is M.4/cycle-complex with the rational Chern character of M.8/motivic-chern-character.
For 2j − i − 1 = 0 use Chow groups and homological equivalence from MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.0 and MC.2/homological-equivalence.

Let a correspondence γ act by pr_{2*}(pr_1^*(−) · γ), using products, flat pullback and proper pushforward of higher Chow groups (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.4 functoriality and products); idempotence of π makes π_* a projector.
acceptance: The definition agrees case by case with Burns–Flach p. 518 and with Bloch–Kato p. 369 (the space W and its subspace Φ).
For X = Spec ℚ, j = 1 the factor H¹_f is 0, while K_1(ℚ) ⊗ ℚ = ℚ^× ⊗ ℚ is infinite-dimensional: the integral part is essential.

nodes.title: Weight vanishing and the shape of the fundamental line
nodes.statement: Let M be a K-theoretic motive datum of weight w. (i) H¹_f(K, M) = 0 if w ≥ 0, and H⁰_f(K, M) = 0 unless w = 0. (ii) If w ≤ −3, all of H⁰_f(K, M), H⁰_f(K, M*(1)) and H¹_f(K, M*(1)) vanish, so the Burns–Flach line is Ξ(M) = d(H¹_f(K,M))⁻¹ · ∏_{v|∞} d(H_v(M)^{G_v})⁻¹ · d(H_dR(M)/F⁰). (iii) If w = −2, only H¹_f(K, M) and H⁰_f(K, M*(1)) can be nonzero. (iv) If w = −1, only H¹_f(K, M) and H¹_f(K, M*(1)) can be nonzero. (v) The statements for w ≥ 0 follow from (ii)–(iv) for M*(1), whose weight is −2 − w.
hypotheses: M is a K-theoretic motive datum; no finiteness is used.
proofSteps: (i) is the case distinction in FL.1/motivic-factor-spaces: 2j − i − 1 < 0 exactly when w ≥ 0, and i = 2j exactly when w = 0.
Apply (i) to M*(1), of weight −2 − w (FL.1/k-theoretic-motive, dualTwist).
Substitute into the formula for Ξ_A(M) of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.3.1 (rational-fundamental-line).
acceptance: For ℚ(2) over ℚ (w = −4): Ξ = d(K_3(ℤ) ⊗ ℚ)⁻¹ · d(B⁺)⁻¹ · d(t) with K_3(ℤ) ⊗ ℚ = 0.
For ℚ(1) over ℚ (w = −2): the surviving motivic factor is H⁰_f(ℚ(0)) = ℚ, as in PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.3, Examples.

nodes.title: Motivic factors of Artin motives
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, E a number field of coefficients and V = e·h⁰(Spec F) ⊗ E an Artin motive over ℚ with coefficients in E (e an idempotent correspondence), and r ∈ ℤ. Then: H⁰_f(V(r)) = 0 for r ≠ 0, and H⁰_f(V) = e(ℚ ⊗ E) (the e-part of CH⁰(Spec F) ⊗ E); H¹_f(V(r)) = 0 for r ≤ 0; for r ≥ 1, H¹_f(V(r)) = e·(K_{2r−1}(O_F) ⊗ E), which for r ≥ 2 equals e·(K_{2r−1}(F) ⊗ E) and for r = 1 equals e·(O_F^× ⊗ E). For V = h⁰(F) and E = ℚ: dim H¹_f(h⁰(F)(1)) = r₁ + r₂ − 1, and for r ≥ 2 dim H¹_f(h⁰(F)(r)) = r₂ if r is even and r₁ + r₂ if r is odd. In general dim_E H¹_f(V(r)) = dim_E V_B(r − 1)^+ − dim_E H⁰_f(V^∨(1 − r)) for r ≥ 1, where (−)^+ is the invariant part under the infinity involution.
hypotheses: F/ℚ finite; E a number field; V a direct summand of h⁰(Spec F) ⊗ E cut out by an idempotent.
proofSteps: K_{2r−1}(F) ⊗ ℚ is pure of Adams weight r for r ≥ 1 (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.6/rational-weight-comparison; BorelRegulators R.4/regulator-adams-products), so the Adams eigenspace in FL.1/motivic-factor-spaces is the whole rational group.

Localization K_{2r−1}(O_F) → K_{2r−1}(F) → ⊕_v K_{2r−2}(k_v) with finite K-groups of finite fields gives K_{2r−1}(O_F) ⊗ ℚ = K_{2r−1}(F) ⊗ ℚ for r ≥ 2 (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/integral-motivic-structures); for r = 1, K_1(O_F) = O_F^×.

Ranks: Borel's theorem (BorelRegulators R.3/borel-rank-theorem) for r ≥ 2 and Dirichlet's unit theorem (Mathlib NumberField.Units.finrank_eq, NumberField.Units.rank) for r = 1; finite generation (ArithmeticKTheory N.3) for the integral groups.
The dimension formula is the dimension count of the exact sequences of FL.2/real-exactness-artin; e commutes with everything by functoriality of K-theory in the field automorphisms.
acceptance: F = ℚ: H¹_f(ℚ(r)) has dimension 1 for odd r ≥ 3 and 0 for even r ≥ 2 and for r = 1 (artinFactorRank_rat).
F imaginary quadratic: dimension 1 for every r ≥ 2 and 0 for r = 1.

Dimension bookkeeping: with artinFactorRank K r the dimension above and tatePlusDim K r = r₁ + r₂ (r even) or r₂ (r odd), artinFactorRank + tatePlusDim = [K:ℚ] for r ≥ 2 and artinFactorRank + 1 + tatePlusDim = [K:ℚ] for r = 1 (artinFactorRank_add_tatePlusDim, artinFactorRank_one_add).

nodes.title: Motivic factors of elliptic motives
nodes.statement: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K with a regular proper flat model ℰ over O_K and Künneth projector π¹, and j ∈ ℤ. Then: (i) H⁰_f(K, h¹(E)(j)) = 0 for all j; (ii) H¹_f(K, h¹(E)(j)) = 0 for j ≤ 0; (iii) H¹_f(K, h¹(E)(1)) = π¹_*(CH¹(E)_{hom∼0} ⊗ ℚ) = E(K) ⊗ ℚ through the Abel–Jacobi map P ↦ [P] − [O], a ℚ-space of dimension rank E(K); (iv) for j ≥ 2, H¹_f(K, h¹(E)(j)) is the π¹-part of the image of (K_{2j−2}(ℰ) ⊗ ℚ)^{(j)} in (K_{2j−2}(E) ⊗ ℚ)^{(j)}; for j = 2 it is the integral part of K₂(E) ⊗ ℚ used by EllipticRegulators ER.6; (v) the Weil pairing identifies h¹(E)^∨ with h¹(E)(1), hence the dual datum h¹(E)(j)*(1) with h¹(E)(2 − j), compatibly with the factors.
hypotheses: ℰ regular proper flat over O_K; for j ≥ 2 finite dimensionality of the factor in (iv) is not known and remains a hypothesis of every determinant formed from it.
proofSteps: (i) and (ii) are FL.1/weight-vanishing with i = 1 and w = 1 − 2j.

(iii): for 2j − i − 1 = 0 the factor is homologically trivial divisor classes; on a curve these are Pic⁰(E), and Pic⁰(E) ≅ E(K) by the Abel–Jacobi map (TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 0); finite generation is the Mordell–Weil theorem (Layer 6).
(iv) is FL.1/motivic-factor-spaces with 2j − i − 1 = 2j − 2 and the model ℰ.
(v): the Weil pairing of TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 2 and the duality of Chow motives (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.1/motives-rigid) give h¹(E)^∨ ≅ h¹(E)(1); twist.
acceptance: For E of rank zero, H¹_f(h¹(E)(1)) = 0 and the weight −1 line has no motivic factor.
The centre of symmetry of j ↦ 2 − j is j = 1, matching L(h¹(E)(j), s) = L(E, s + j) and the functional equation s + j ↦ 2 − (s + j).

sources.match: For an abelian variety A the motive M = [0 → A] is self-dual after the twist, its H¹_f is A(ℚ) ⊗ ℚ, and the remaining structure is a nondegenerate pairing identified with the Néron–Tate height.
For an abelian variety the Kummer sequence embeds A(K) ⊗ ℤ_p into H¹_f(K, T), the realization of the weight −1 factor.
The case 2r − n − 1 = 0 of the definition, by homologically trivial cycles.

nodes.title: Real Deligne complex of a motive
nodes.statement: For a K-theoretic motive datum M put H_v(M) = π·H^i(σX(ℂ), (2πi)^j ℚ) for the archimedean place v = v(σ), with G_v = Gal(ℂ/K_v) acting through the infinity involution and complex conjugation of coefficients, B⁺(M) = ⊕_{v|∞} H_v(M)^{G_v}, and t_M = H_dR(M)/F⁰ with the Hodge filtration shifted by j. Define the real Deligne complex RΓ_D(K, M) = [B⁺(M) ⊗ ℝ --α_M--> t_M ⊗_ℚ ℝ] in degrees 0 and 1, where α_M is induced by the comparison H_v(M) ⊗ ℂ ≅ H_dR(M) ⊗_{K,σ} ℂ. Then: (a) α_M is injective if w ≤ −1; (b) α_M is surjective if w ≥ −1; (c) ker(α_M)^* ≅ coker(α_{M*(1)}) and coker(α_M)^* ≅ ker(α_{M*(1)}) canonically; (d) for w ≤ −2, coker α_M is the G_ℝ-invariant real Deligne cohomology H^{i+1}_D(X_{/ℝ}, ℝ(j))_π, of dimension dim t_M − dim B⁺(M); (e) for an Artin motive V(r) with r ≥ 1, coker α = V_dR(r)_ℝ / V_B(r)^+_ℝ ≅ V_B(r − 1)^+_ℝ via ℂ = ℝ ⊕ ℝ(−1).
hypotheses: X smooth projective over K; the comparison isomorphisms and the infinity involution are those of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.0.1–PS.0.2 and MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2.
proofSteps: Form B⁺ and t_M from the realizations of MC.2 (betti-realization, de-rham-motivic comparison) and the infinity involution of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.0/real-infinity; α_M is the composite B⁺ ⊗ ℝ → H_dR ⊗ ℝ → t_M ⊗ ℝ.
(a)–(b): by Hodge symmetry, a real class in F⁰ lies in F⁰ ∩ conj(F⁰) = ⊕_{p,q≥0} H^{p,q}, which is zero in weight w < 0; for w ≥ −1 apply (a) to M*(1) and (c).
(c): Poincaré duality pairs B⁺(M) with B⁺(M*(1)) and F⁰ with F^1 of the dual (Burns–Flach Lemma 18, cited p. 519).

nodes.title: Beilinson regulator sequence
nodes.statement: For a K-theoretic motive datum M define the sequence of finite-dimensional real A_ℝ-modules (when the factors are finite-dimensional) 0 → H⁰_f(K,M)_ℝ --ε--> ker α_M --r_B^*--> H¹_f(K,M*(1))^*_ℝ --δ--> H¹_f(K,M)_ℝ --r_B--> coker α_M --ε^*--> H⁰_f(K,M*(1))^*_ℝ → 0, where ε is the Betti cycle class (landing in ker α_M because algebraic classes lie in F⁰ after the twist), r_B is the Beilinson regulator: the Deligne regulator of MotivicEtaleKTheory §§12.2–12.3 on the Adams eigenspace, composed with π and with delignePeriodMap_coker_eq_deligne (zero when w = −1, where coker α_M = 0), r_B^* and ε^* are the transposes of the corresponding maps for M*(1) under delignePeriodMap_ker_dual, and δ is the height pairing, defined in weight −1 only; for h¹(E)(1) it is the Néron–Tate pairing on E(K) ⊗ ℝ, and for other weight −1 data it is a supplied datum.
hypotheses: Finite dimensionality of the factors where real determinants are later taken.
In weight −1 other than h¹ of an elliptic curve, the height pairing δ is part of the data: no roadmap constructs the Beilinson–Bloch height in general.
proofSteps: Cycle class: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2/chern-character-cycle-map and the Betti realization, followed by the projection to ker α_M.

Regulator: MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/deligne-regulator with its number-field normalization M.8/number-field-deligne-normalization, restricted to the integral part of FL.1/motivic-factor-spaces and composed with the identification of FL.2/deligne-period-complex(d).
Dual maps: apply the same constructions to M*(1) and transpose through FL.2/deligne-period-complex(c).
Height: for h¹(E)(1), the canonical height pairing of TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 6 extended to E(K) ⊗ ℝ, under the identification of FL.1/elliptic-motive-factors(iii) and its self-duality.
acceptance: For h⁰(F)(1): r_B(u) = (log|u|_v)_{v|∞} with |·|_v the normalized absolute value (square at complex places), and ε^* is the sum map; their composite vanishes by the product formula for units.
For ℚ(1) over ℚ the sequence is 0 → 0 → ℝ → ℝ → 0.

nodes.title: Real exactness predicate
nodes.statement: RealExactness(M) is the proposition that the factors H⁰_f, H¹_f of M and of M*(1) are finite-dimensional and the Beilinson regulator sequence of FL.2/real-regulator-sequence is exact, with its ℝ-dual identified with the sequence for M*(1) (Burns–Flach Conjecture 1). By FL.1/weight-vanishing it says: for w ≤ −3, r_B is an isomorphism H¹_f(K,M)_ℝ ≅ coker α_M; for w = −2, 0 → H¹_f(K,M)_ℝ → coker α_M → H⁰_f(K,M*(1))^*_ℝ → 0 is exact; for w = −1, δ is an isomorphism; for w ≥ 0, the dual statements for M*(1).
hypotheses: The maps are those constructed in FL.2/real-regulator-sequence; another choice of maps between the same spaces does not witness the predicate.
proofSteps: Unfold FL.1/weight-vanishing in each weight range.
The duality clause is delignePeriodMap_ker_dual and realRegulatorSequence_dual.
acceptance: RealExactness(ℚ(1) over ℚ) holds trivially.
RealExactness(M) ↔ RealExactness(M*(1)).

nodes.title: Real exactness for Artin motives
nodes.statement: For every Artin motive V over ℚ with coefficients in a number field E and every r ∈ ℤ, RealExactness(V(r)) holds. Explicitly: for r ≥ 1 the sequence 0 → H¹_f(V(r))_ℝ --r_B--> V_B(r − 1)^+_ℝ → H⁰_f(V^∨(1 − r))^∨_ℝ → 0 is exact (the last term vanishes unless r = 1), and for r ≤ 0 the sequence 0 → H⁰_f(V(r))_ℝ --ε--> V_B(r)^+_ℝ → H¹_f(V^∨(1 − r))^∨_ℝ → 0 is exact.
hypotheses: V a direct summand of h⁰(Spec F) ⊗ E.
proofSteps: r ≥ 2: Borel's theorem that the Borel regulator is an isomorphism K_{2r−1}(F) ⊗ ℝ ≅ V_r(F) (BorelRegulators R.4/regulator-real-isomorphism), the comparison Borel = 2·Beilinson in the same Tate coordinates (R.7/regulator-factor-two), and the identification of V_r(F) with coker α (FL.2/deligne-period-complex(e)); apply the idempotent e by Galois equivariance (R.4/regulator-transfer).

r = 1: Dirichlet's unit theorem: the logarithmic embedding of O_F^× ⊗ ℝ is an isomorphism onto the trace-zero hyperplane of ⊕_{v|∞} ℝ (Mathlib NumberField.Units.logEmbedding, NumberField.Units.finrank_eq, NumberField.Units.regulator_pos), and the quotient by the hyperplane is H⁰_f(h⁰(F))^∨_ℝ = ℝ via the sum.
r ≤ 0: dualize the cases 1 − r ≥ 1 with FL.2/real-exactness (realExactness_dual).
acceptance: For F = ℚ and r = 3: the regulator of the generator of K_5(ℤ) ⊗ ℚ is a nonzero multiple of ζ(3) times a rational power of π, consistent with dim coker α = 1.
For F real quadratic and r = 1: the exact sequence is 0 → ℝ log ε₀ → ℝ² → ℝ → 0.

sources.match: The real isomorphism of the fundamental line of an Artin motive is induced by the two short exact sequences, by twist r ≤ 0 and r ≥ 1, built from the cycle map and the Beilinson regulator; the regulator is an isomorphism for r > 1 by Borel and Rapoport.
For the unit motive and for 𝔾_m over F the sequence reduces to the logarithmic unit regulator and its transpose; the resulting statements are the class number formula.

nodes.title: Real exactness for elliptic motives
nodes.statement: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K. (i) RealExactness(h¹(E)(1)) holds: α_M is an isomorphism, the H⁰ factors vanish, H¹_f(K,M) = H¹_f(K,M*(1)) = E(K) ⊗ ℚ, and δ is the Néron–Tate pairing, which is positive definite on E(K) ⊗ ℝ. (ii) For j ≥ 2, RealExactness(h¹(E)(j)) is equivalent to: H¹_f(K, h¹(E)(j)) is finite-dimensional and r_B ⊗ ℝ is an isomorphism onto H²_D(E_{/ℝ}, ℝ(j)), of real dimension [K:ℚ]. For K = ℚ and j = 2 this is the rational form of EllipticRegulators ER.6/the-beilinson-statement. (iii) For j ≤ 0, RealExactness(h¹(E)(j)) ↔ RealExactness(h¹(E)(2 − j)).
hypotheses: (i) uses Mordell–Weil over K and the Néron–Tate height; (ii) is an equivalence, not an assertion: no case of j ≥ 2 is proved here.
proofSteps: (i): by FL.2/deligne-period-complex (a)–(b) in weight −1, α_M is an isomorphism; FL.1/elliptic-motive-factors gives the factors; the sequence reduces to δ, which is the Néron–Tate pairing; positive definiteness on E(K) ⊗ ℝ (TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 6) gives exactness.

(ii): weight 1 − 2j ≤ −3, so FL.2/real-exactness reduces to bijectivity of r_B; since F^j H¹_dR(E) = 0 for j ≥ 2, t_M = H¹_dR(E/K) has ℚ-dimension 2[K:ℚ], while B⁺ has dimension r₁ + 2r₂ = [K:ℚ] (one eigenline of the infinity involution at each real place, the full plane at each complex place), so dim coker α_M = [K:ℚ]; for K = ℚ and j = 2 compare with ER.6.
(iii): FL.2/real-exactness, realExactness_dual, with FL.1/elliptic-motive-factors(v).
acceptance: For E/ℚ of rank zero, (i) is the statement that 0 → 0 is exact and α_M is the real period isomorphism.
For E/ℚ of rank one generated by P, δ is multiplication by the canonical height ĥ(P) > 0.

nodes.title: Fundamental-line real comparison
nodes.statement: For a K-theoretic motive datum M with RealExactness(M), define fundamentalLineRealComparison(M) = ϑ_∞(M) : Ξ_A(M) ⊗ ℝ ≅ 1, the trivialization realTrivialization of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.3.2 applied to the exact sequence of FL.2/real-regulator-sequence together with 0 → ker α_M → B⁺_ℝ → t_{M,ℝ} → coker α_M → 0, in the fixed order of factors of Ξ_A(M). For an Artin motive V(r) with integral Betti lattice T_B and a ℤ-lattice Ω ⊂ H¹_f(V(r)) (the image of K_{2r−1}(O_F) modulo torsion), the coordinate of ϑ_∞ on det⁻¹ Ω ⊗ det⁻¹ T_B(r)^+ ⊗ det t_M is the Beilinson regulator covolume of Ω in V_B(r − 1)^+_ℝ relative to T_B, times the comparison factor of PS.0; for h⁰(F)(1 − k), k ≥ 2, ϑ_∞ sends a generator of det⁻¹ Ω ⊗ det⁻¹ T_B(1 − k)^+ to ±R_k(F)⁻¹, where R_k(F) is the Beilinson regulator covolume of Ω.
hypotheses: RealExactness(M); the factors finite-dimensional and, for coefficients A, projective.
proofSteps: Apply PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.3/real-regulator-trivialization with the maps of FL.2/real-regulator-sequence as its exact-sequence witness; the archimedean comparison is PS.0/comparison-period-line.

Coordinates: in chosen bases, multiplicativity of determinants along the two exact sequences gives the signed regulator determinant times the comparison determinant (Mathlib Matrix.det, Matrix.det_smul); for Artin motives follow Huber–Kings Proposition 1.2.3 and the proof of Theorem 1.4.1.
Compare with Borel's normalization by BorelRegulators R.4/regulator-covolume and R.7/regulator-factor-two.
acceptance: The ordered determinant identifications are those of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §5.1, so the comparison is defined on graded lines.
ϑ_∞(M*(1)) is the dual of ϑ_∞(M) under Ξ(M*(1)) ≅ Ξ(M)^* ⊗ (archimedean and de Rham factors), as in Huber–Kings Proposition 2.2.3.

nodes.title: p-adic realization of motivic factors
nodes.statement: For a K-theoretic motive datum M and a prime p, with V_p = π·H^i_et(X_K̄, ℚ_p(j)) (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2/etale-realization), define c⁰_p : H⁰_f(K,M) ⊗ ℚ_p → H⁰(K, V_p) by the p-adic cycle class (i = 2j), and c¹_p : H¹_f(K,M) ⊗ ℚ_p → H¹(K, V_p) as follows: if 2j − i − 1 > 0, apply the normalized étale Chern character of K_{2j−i−1}(X)^{(j)} into H^{i+1}_et(X, ℚ_p(j)) (MotivicEtaleKTheory §12.1 and Layer 9) and the Hochschild–Serre edge, whose obstruction term H^{i+1}(X_K̄, ℚ_p(j))^{G_K} vanishes because i + 1 ≠ 2j and the Weil conjectures exclude the weight; if 2j − i − 1 = 0, use the p-adic Abel–Jacobi map on homologically trivial cycles (the Kummer map for h¹(E)(1)). The image of the integral part lies in the Bloch–Kato group H¹_g(K, V_p) (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/selmer-regulator-factorization and PadicHodgeRegulators D.2); it lies in H¹_f(K, V_p) = H¹RΓ_f(K, V_p) whenever H¹_f = H¹_g locally at each v | p, in particular for Artin motives of twist ≥ 1, for h¹(E)(1), and for every M of weight ≤ −3 with good reduction at p, and as a hypothesis otherwise.
hypotheses: p any prime; S a finite set of places containing the archimedean places, the places of bad reduction and the places above p.
Outside the listed cases the inclusion of the image in H¹_f(K, V_p) is a hypothesis of every statement using c¹_p.
proofSteps: Étale Chern character: MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/finite-etale-chern with the rational normalization of M.8/motivic-chern-character and the comparison M.8/chern-functoriality; pass to ℚ_p-coefficients through continuous cohomology (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7/arithmetic-adic-degrees).
Edge map: Hochschild–Serre for X → Spec K; the weight argument of Bloch–Kato (5.2), p. 370.

Local conditions: the Bloch–Kato conditions of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4/bloch-kato-condition, the global Selmer group L2/galois-selmer-group, and the syntomic factorization of PadicHodgeRegulators D.2/syntomic-etale-regulator-comparison for the image in H¹_g; H¹_f = H¹_g in weights ≤ −3 at good p because D_cris(V_p^*(1))^{φ=1} = 0 by purity of Frobenius weights (Bloch–Kato Proposition 3.8 and Corollary 3.8.4, pp. 354–355).
acceptance: For h⁰(F)(1), c¹_p is the Kummer map O_F^× ⊗ ℚ_p → H¹_f(F, ℚ_p(1)), compatible with Tau Ceti's TauCeti.kummerMap on finite levels.
Weight argument check: for X = Spec F, H^{i+1}(X_K̄, ℚ_p(j))^{G_K} = H¹ of a point is zero, so the edge map is defined without hypotheses.

nodes.title: p-adic realization for Artin motives
nodes.statement: For every Artin motive V over ℚ with coefficients in E, every r ∈ ℤ and every prime p, PadicRealizationIso(V(r), p) holds. In twist r ≥ 2 this is Soulé's theorem that K_{2r−1}(O_F) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ H¹(O_F[1/p], ℚ_p(r)) = H¹_f(F, ℚ_p(r)), together with H²(O_F[1/p], ℚ_p(r)) = 0; in twist 1 it is Kummer theory O_F^× ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ H¹_f(F, ℚ_p(1)); in twists r ≤ 0 it follows by duality.
hypotheses: V a direct summand of h⁰(Spec F) ⊗ E; p arbitrary (at p = 2 only the rational statements are used).
proofSteps: r ≥ 2, p odd: MotivicEtaleKTheory §10.5 (M.7/arithmetic-adic-degrees) identifies the p-completed K-groups of O_F[1/p] with H¹ and H² of ℤ_p(r); finite generation (ArithmeticKTheory N.3) identifies them with K_n(O_F[1/p]) ⊗ ℤ_p; Borel's ranks (BorelRegulators R.3/borel-rank-theorem) give K_{2r−2}(O_F) ⊗ ℚ = 0, hence H²(ℚ_p(r)) = 0; localization identifies O_F[1/p] with O_F rationally for r ≥ 2.
p = 2: the same rational statements follow from the dyadic comparisons of MotivicEtaleKTheory Layer 11 (M.7/dyadic-s-integer-extensions), whose real-place corrections are 2-torsion.
Local conditions: for r ≥ 2 the local H¹_f equals H¹ at v | p and the unramified condition is automatic rationally at v ∤ p (Bloch–Kato Example 3.9), so H¹_f(F, ℚ_p(r)) = H¹(O_F[1/p], ℚ_p(r)).
r = 1: Kummer theory and finiteness of the class group (Bloch–Kato Example 3.9 and p. 358; Huber–Kings p. 6).
r ≤ 0: PadicRealizationIso is self-dual (FL.3/padic-realization-iso); 1 − r ≥ 1. Apply the idempotent by Galois equivariance.
acceptance: For F = ℚ and r = 3, both sides are one-dimensional over ℚ_p.
For r = 0 and V = h⁰(F): c⁰_p : ℚ ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ H⁰(F, ℚ_p) = ℚ_p.

Its image is H¹_f(K, V_pE) exactly when the divisible part of Sha[p^∞] vanishes (Bloch–Kato Proposition 5.4 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology L4/elliptic-finite-kummer); as Sha[p^∞] is cofinitely generated, this is finiteness.

nodes.title: Selmer complex cohomology of Artin motives
nodes.statement: Let V be an Artin motive over ℚ with coefficients in E, S a finite set of primes and p a prime. The Selmer complex RΓ_f(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p(r)) (global cochains with the Bloch–Kato conditions at Sp) is: for r > 1, concentrated in degree 1 with H¹ = H¹(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p(r)); for r = 1, concentrated in degrees 1 and 3, with a triangle H¹_f(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p(1))[−1] → RΓ_f → H⁰(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p^∨)^∨[−3]; for r < 0, concentrated in degree 2 with H² ≅ H¹(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p^∨(1 − r))^∨; for r = 0, concentrated in degrees 0 and 2, with a triangle H⁰(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p) → RΓ_f → H¹_f(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p^∨(1))^∨[−2]. Moreover there is a canonical triangle RΓ_c(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p(r)) → RΓ_f(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p(r)) → V_p(r)^+ ⊕ ⊕_{v∈Sp} RΓ_f(ℚ_v, V_p(r)).
hypotheses: V Artin; the vanishing H²(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p(r)) = 0 for r > 1 is supplied by FL.3/padic-realization-artin.
proofSteps: Use the Poitou–Tate sequence for RΓ_f (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/poitou-tate and SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2/selmer-structure-poitou-tate) with the duality of the Bloch–Kato conditions.
Insert the local dimensions of Bloch–Kato Example 3.9 and the global vanishing of H² in twists > 1 (FL.3/padic-realization-artin).
The final triangle is the vertical triangle of the nine-term diagram (Burns–Flach (26)) with the archimedean term V_p(r)^+.
acceptance: For V = ℚ and r = 2: RΓ_f has H¹ = H¹(ℤ[1/Sp], ℚ_p(2)) = 0 and is acyclic.
For V = ℚ and r = 0: H⁰ = ℚ_p and H² = H¹_f(ℚ, ℚ_p(1))^∨ = 0.

nodes.title: Fundamental-line p-adic comparison
nodes.statement: For a K-theoretic motive datum M with coefficients in A, a prime p, a finite set S of places of K containing S_∞ and the bad places, and assuming PadicRealizationIso(M, p), define fundamentalLinePadicComparison(M, S) = ϑ_p(M, S) : Ξ_A(M) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ d_{A_p} RΓ_c(O_{K,S_p}, V_p), the isomorphism obtained by applying the determinant functor to: the realization isomorphisms c^i_p(M), i = 0, 1, 2, 3 (FL.3/padic-realization-iso); the Betti–étale comparison (H_v(M) ⊗ ℚ_p)^{G_v} ≅ H⁰(K_v, V_p) at v | ∞; the de Rham comparison (H_dR(M)/F⁰) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ ⊕_{v|p} t_v(V_p); the local trivializations of RΓ_f(K_v, V_p) at v ∈ S_{p,f} by the identity isomorphism [V → V] ≅ 1 (not the acyclic trivialization); and the vertical triangle RΓ_c → RΓ_f(K, V_p) → ⊕_{v∈S_p} RΓ_f(K_v, V_p). For an Artin motive V(r) over ℚ it is the isomorphism Δ_f(V(r)) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ det RΓ_c(ℤ[1/Sp], V_p(r)) of Huber–Kings Definition 1.2.7, and at p the identity trivialization differs from the acyclic one by the Euler factor P_p(V, p^{−r}).
hypotheses: PadicRealizationIso(M, p); finite projectivity of the factors over A_p.
At p = 2 with real places of K the compact-support complex is the modified one of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4.4; integral statements are not made there.
proofSteps: Global and compact-support cochains with their perfectness: ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7/compact-support-cochains, D7/cochain-finiteness-perfectness; the Selmer complex and its condition-change triangles: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2/selmer-complex, L2/condition-change-triangle.
Archimedean terms: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.2/etale-betti-motivic-comparison; de Rham terms: PadicHodgeTheory R06.5/proper-smooth-de-rham-comparison.

Local determinant identifications at v ∤ p and v | p, including the Euler factors: PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4/local-correction-adapter; the comparison of the identity and acyclic trivializations is Huber–Kings Proposition 1.2.5.
Assemble with the determinant functor of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §5.1 (stage L5), in the fixed order of Ξ.
acceptance: Independence of S: enlarging S by w ∤ p changes RΓ_c by the cone of [V^{I_w} → V^{I_w}], trivialized compatibly (Burns–Flach Lemma 5; Huber–Kings Proposition 1.2.9(b)).
For V = ℚ, r = 1 − k with k ≥ 2: the Euler factor at p is ∏_{v|p}(1 − N(v)^{k−1}), a p-adic unit.

nodes.title: Tamagawa condition for K-theoretic motives
nodes.statement: Let M be a K-theoretic motive datum over ℚ (restricting scalars if necessary) with coefficients in a number field E, O = O_E, with RealExactness(M) and PadicRealizationIso(M, p), and let L*(M, 0) ∈ (E ⊗ ℝ)^× be the leading coefficient at s = 0 of its finite L-function (PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.3.3). Let δ(M) ∈ Ξ_E(M) ⊗ ℝ be the unique element with ϑ_∞(L*(M,0) · δ(M)) = 1. For a Galois-stable O_p-lattice T_p ⊂ V_p, TamagawaCondition(M, T_p, p) is the proposition: δ(M) lies in the rational line Ξ_E(M), and ϑ_p(M, S)(δ(M)) is an O_p-generator of d_{O_p} RΓ_c(O_{K,S_p}, T_p) ⊂ d_{E_p} RΓ_c(O_{K,S_p}, V_p). Equivalently, in Kato's orientation with Δ = Ξ⁻¹: there is an E-basis ζ(M) of Δ_E(M) whose real image is L*(M, 0) and whose p-adic image is an O_p-basis of d⁻¹_{O_p} RΓ_c(T_p), namely ζ(M) = δ(M)^{⊗(−1)}.
hypotheses: RealExactness(M) and PadicRealizationIso(M, p); the L-function has an analytic continuation to s = 0 with a nonzero leading coefficient, supplied by its owner (for Artin motives BorelRegulators R.5 and the trivial-character interface; otherwise a hypothesis).
p odd, or K without real places, unless a bounded perfect replacement at 2 is supplied (PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4.4).
proofSteps: Uniqueness of δ: Ξ_E(M) ⊗ ℝ is free of rank one over E ⊗ ℝ and ϑ_∞ is an isomorphism (FL.2/fundamental-line-real-comparison).
Rationality is the predicate LeadingTermRational of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.3/leading-term-line for the comparison of FL.2.

The integral clause uses ϑ_p of FL.3/fundamental-line-padic-comparison and the integral inverse determinant Δ_p(T) = det⁻¹ RΓ_c(T_p) of MotivicEtaleKTheory §12.7 (M.8/arithmetic-fundamental-line, its Δ_p(T) part).
Kato's orientation: d(C)⁻¹ = d(C)^{−1} and Δ = Ξ⁻¹ (PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.3.1), so a generator of one lattice is the inverse of a generator of the other.
acceptance: The condition depends only on the O_p^×-orbit of δ: units do not change generation.
For E = ℚ and T_p = ℤ_p the condition says ϑ_p(δ) ∈ ℤ_p^× · (a generator) of the lattice.

nodes.title: Tamagawa condition and the commutative Tamagawa obstruction
nodes.statement: Let M be a K-theoretic motive datum with commutative coefficients E, O = O_E, satisfying RealExactness(M) and PadicRealizationIso(M, p) for every p in a set Σ of odd primes. Take θ_∞ = ϑ_∞(M) and θ_p = ϑ_p(M, S) in PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4.1 and PS.5.1. Then TamagawaCondition(M, T_p, p) holds for every p ∈ Σ if and only if the p-parts, p ∈ Σ, of the commutative Tamagawa obstruction TΩ(M, O) of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.5.2 vanish, that is, θ_∞ carries the λ-adic lattice I_p(M, T, S) of PS.4.1 onto (L*)⁻¹ · O_p for each p ∈ Σ; and, for Σ the set of all odd primes, if and only if the Fukaya–Kato zeta isomorphism orientation of PS.5.3 is satisfied with these comparisons.

nodes.title: Lattice, place-set, duality and Selmer forms of the condition
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of FL.4/tamagawa-condition: (a) TamagawaCondition(M, T_p, p) does not depend on the Galois-stable lattice T_p nor on the finite set S containing the bad places; (b) for p odd, the integral structures d RΓ_c(O_{K,S_p}, T_p) ⊗ d(T_p^+) and d RΓ(O_{K,S_p}, T_p^∨(1)) agree under global duality, so the condition can be stated with RΓ(O_{K,S_p}, T_p^∨(1)) in place of RΓ_c (Kato's formulation for twists of the dual); at p = 2 the complex RΓ is replaced by τ_{≤2}RΓ and T_p^+ by Tate cohomology; (c) with the Selmer mapping fibre C_f(T_p) and local conditions U_v^+, the local determinant formula det⁻¹ C_f ≅ det⁻¹ C_c ⊗ ⊗_v det⁻¹ U_v^+ of MotivicEtaleKTheory §12.7 and the local Euler and Tamagawa identifications of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4.3 turn the condition into: ϑ_p(δ), tensored with the generators of the lattices d U_v^+ (v ∈ S_p) given by their local identifications, generates the lattice d_{O_p} C_f(T_p) of the Selmer complex. This is the local correction in the Tate and elliptic Tamagawa statements.
hypotheses: As in FL.4/tamagawa-condition; (b) and (c) for p odd unless the dyadic replacement of PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4.4 is supplied.
proofSteps: (a): for T′ ⊂ T the finite quotient has Euler characteristic of RΓ_c equal to 1 (Tate's formula; ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/global-euler-characteristic), so the lattices agree (PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4/finite-lattice-correction; Burns–Flach Lemma 5). For S ⊂ S′ use the localization triangle with RΓ(F_v, T^{I_v}) and its compatibility with FL.3/fundamental-line-padic-comparison (fundamentalLinePadicComparison_enlargeS).

(b): derived Poitou–Tate duality RΓ_c(T) ≅ RHom(RΓ(T^∨(1)), O_p)[−3] up to the archimedean term (ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7/derived-global-duality); compare d(A ⊗^L E_p/O_p)^* with d⁻¹(A) (Huber–Kings Proposition 1.2.10).

(c): apply MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/selmer-local-determinant-comparison to the triangle C_c → C_f → ⊕_v U_v^+ and PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.4/local-correction-adapter to identify each det⁻¹ U_v^+ with the Euler or Tamagawa factor.
acceptance: For T′ = pT the two lattices d RΓ_c(T′) and d RΓ_c(T) coincide, although each cohomology group changes.
With every U_v^+ = 0 the Selmer form is the compact-support form.

sources.locator: Propositions 1.2.9 and 1.2.10 with the following remarks, pp. 10–11
sources.match: Independence of the lattice by the Euler characteristic of RΓ_c of a finite module, independence of S by the localization sequence, and agreement of the integral structures under global duality for p ≠ 2, with the modification at p = 2.
Independence of the object Ξ(M, T_p, S) of the lattice and of S.
Determinants of perfect complexes, multiplicativity on distinguished triangles and the compactly supported cohomology removing p and ∞.

nodes.title: Class number formula case
nodes.statement: For every number field F and every odd prime p, TamagawaCondition(h⁰(F), ℤ_p, p) and TamagawaCondition(h⁰(F)(1), ℤ_p(1), p) hold. In twist 0, Ξ(h⁰(F)) = d(ℚ) ⊗ d(O_F^× ⊗ ℚ)⁻¹ ⊗ d(T_B^+ ⊗ ℚ)⁻¹, the element δ is (R_∞(F)/ζ_F^*(0)) times the integral generator and ζ_F^*(0) = −h_F R_F/w_F; the integral condition is the Poitou–Tate sequence relating O_F^× ⊗ ℤ_p, H¹ and H² of O_F[1/p] with ℤ_p(1), the local quotients H¹/H¹_f at p and Cl(O_F) ⊗ ℤ_p. In twist 1, L*(h⁰(F)(1), 0) is the residue of ζ_F at s = 1, 2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂} h_F R_F / (w_F √|d_F|) (Mathlib NumberField.dedekindZeta_residue), and the condition follows from twist 0 by the functional equation and the local computation at p that the Bloch–Kato exponential carries O_{F_v} onto a subgroup of index (q_v − 1)/q_v in O_{F_v}^× ⊗ ℤ_p.
hypotheses: p odd (the statement up to powers of 2).
The functional equation and leading coefficient of ζ_F at s = 0 are supplied by the trivial-character interface (BorelRegulators R.5); the residue at s = 1 is Mathlib's.
proofSteps: Twist 0: the real comparison of FL.2/real-exactness-artin (r = 0) with the regulator R_∞(F) of the unit lattice and the section s_∞; insert ζ_F^*(0) = −h_F R_F/w_F (BorelRegulators R.5/completed-zeta-conventions and R.5/leading-term-functional-equation for the functional-equation input; Mathlib NumberField.dedekindZeta_residue and NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT at s = 1).

The Poitou–Tate sequence 0 → O_F^× ⊗ ℤ_p → H¹(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(1)) → H¹_{/f}(F ⊗ ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)) → Cl(O_F) ⊗ ℤ_p → H²(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(1)) → H²(F ⊗ ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)) → H⁰(O_F[1/p], ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^* → 0 (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/poitou-tate) gives the determinant of RΓ(ℤ[1/p], T^∨(1)); combine with FL.4/tamagawa-condition-alternative-forms(b) and the identification of the local lattice det⁻¹ RΓ_{/f}(F ⊗ ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)) with ℤ_p.

Twist 1: the ratio ζ_F^*(0)/ζ_F^*(1) = ±√|d_F|/(2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂}) from the functional equation; the de Rham lattice O_F and the Betti lattices differ by the same factor; the exponential index (1 − 1/q_v) at each v | p is the Euler factor of FL.3/fundamental-line-padic-comparison (fundamentalLinePadicComparison_eulerFactor).
acceptance: F = ℚ, twist 0: ζ(0) = −1/2, h = 1, R = 1, w = 2; the condition at odd p is v_p(1/2) = 0.

F real quadratic, twist 1: L* = 2h_F R_F/√d_F and δ = ±(2h_F)⁻¹ times the integral generator (FL.2/fundamental-line-real-comparison, test); the integral clause at odd p is v_p(h_F) = v_p(#Cl(O_F) ⊗ ℤ_p).

sources.locator: Proposition 2.3.1 and its proof, Proposition 2.3.2, pp. 18–21
sources.match: The Bloch–Kato conjecture for h⁰(F) in twists 0 and 1 up to powers of 2: twist 0 from the analytic class number formula at s = 0 and the Poitou–Tate sequence with units and class group; twist 1 by the functional equation and the index of the exponential at p.
For the unit motive and 𝔾_m over F the Bloch–Kato conjecture reduces to the class number formula at s = 0 and at s = 1.

nodes.title: Cohomological Lichtenbaum form
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, k ≥ 2 and p an odd prime. Let R_k(F) be the Beilinson regulator covolume of K_{2k−1}(O_F)/tors in V_B(k − 1)^+_ℝ relative to the integral Betti lattice. Then TamagawaCondition(h⁰(F)(1 − k), ℤ_p(1 − k), p) holds if and only if the p-adic valuations satisfy v_p(ζ_F^*(1 − k)/R_k(F)) = v_p(#H²(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(k))) − v_p(#H¹(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(k))_tors), where ζ_F^*(1 − k)/R_k(F) ∈ ℚ^× by Borel's theorem and the Beilinson comparison. Consequently the Tamagawa condition for h⁰(F)(1 − k) at all odd p is equivalent to the odd part of the cohomological Lichtenbaum formula |ζ_F^*(1 − k)| = R_k(F) · ∏_p #H²(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(k)) / #H¹(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(k))_tors.
hypotheses: p odd; k ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Ξ(h⁰(F)(1 − k)) = d⁻¹ H¹_f(h⁰(F)(k)) ⊗ d⁻¹ T_B(1 − k)^+ by FL.1/weight-vanishing and FL.1/artin-motive-factors; ϑ_∞ sends the integral generator to ±R_k(F)⁻¹ (FL.2/fundamental-line-real-comparison), so δ_ℤ = ±(R_k(F)/ζ_F^*(1 − k)) times that generator.

RΓ_f(ℤ[1/p], V_p(1 − k)) ≅ H¹(ℤ[1/p], V_p^∨(k))^∨[−2] by FL.3/selmer-complex-cohomology-artin; the local Euler factor at p is ∏_{v|p}(1 − N(v)^{k−1}), a p-adic unit (FL.3/fundamental-line-padic-comparison).

By FL.4/tamagawa-condition-alternative-forms(b) the condition says (R_k/ζ^*) ℤ_p = det r_p(Ω ⊗ ℤ_p) ⊗ det RΓ(ℤ[1/p], T^∨(k)); Soulé's surjectivity with Borel's ranks (FL.3/padic-realization-artin, through MotivicEtaleKTheory §10.5) identifies r_p(Ω ⊗ ℤ_p) with the free part of H¹(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(k)); a finite ℤ_p-module of order h has determinant h⁻¹ℤ_p.
Rationality of ζ_F^*(1 − k)/R_k(F): BorelRegulators R.5/borel-zeta-proportionality and R.7/regulator-factor-two.
acceptance: F = ℚ, k = 2: ζ(−1) = −1/12, R_2(ℚ) = 1, H²(ℤ[1/p], ℤ_p(2)) is the p-part of K₂(ℤ) = ℤ/2 (trivial at odd p) and H¹(ℤ[1/p], ℤ_p(2))_tors is the p-part of w₂(ℚ) = 24; at p = 3 both sides are −1.
F totally real and k even: rank zero, R_k = 1, and the formula is |ζ_F(1 − k)| = ∏_p #H² / #H¹_tors at odd p, the statement SpecialValuesBirchTate consumes.

sources.match: The Bloch–Kato conjecture for h⁰(F) at 1 − k implies, up to sign and powers of 2, ζ_F(1 − k)* = R_k(F) ∏_p #H²(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(k)) / #H¹(O_F[1/p], ℤ_p(k))_tors; the proof runs through the duality form, the unit Euler factor and Soulé's surjectivity with Borel's ranks, and each step is reversible.

nodes.title: Elliptic fundamental-line data
nodes.statement: For an elliptic curve E over ℚ and an odd prime p with Sha(E/ℚ)[p^∞] finite, the K-theoretic data of h¹(E)(1) (FL.1/elliptic-motive-factors, FL.2/real-exactness-elliptic, FL.3/padic-realization-elliptic) are the regulator, Kummer and Tamagawa identifications that PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.6.3 takes as hypotheses: H¹_f = E(ℚ) ⊗ ℚ with the Néron–Tate height as δ, α_M the real period isomorphism, and ϑ_p built from the Kummer isomorphism E(ℚ) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ H¹_f(ℚ, V_pE). Hence TamagawaCondition(h¹(E)(1), T_pE, p) is equivalent to the p-part of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula, by PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.6/elliptic-fundamental-adapter.
hypotheses: E/ℚ, p odd, Sha(E/ℚ)[p^∞] finite; the analytic leading term of L(E, s) at s = 1 is supplied by its owner (modularity, TauCetiRoadmap ModularForms through PeriodsAndSpecialValues).
proofSteps: Supply the three identifications from FL.1–FL.3.
Apply PS.6/elliptic-fundamental-adapter (ellipticFundamentalLine_iff_bsd), whose hypotheses are exactly these identifications, and PS.6/bsd-prime-assembly for the prime-by-prime form.
acceptance: For E/ℚ of rank zero with L(E, 1) ≠ 0 the statement is the p-part of L(E,1)/Ω_E = #Sha · ∏ c_ℓ / #E(ℚ)_tors².
For rank one, the height determinant of a generator P is ĥ(P), and replacing P by 3P multiplies it by 9.

sources.match: For an abelian variety the conjunction of the order-of-vanishing and Bloch–Kato statements is equivalent to the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, once Sha is finite.
The Kummer realization of A(K) ⊗ ℤ_p in H¹_f(K, T) and its surjectivity under finiteness of the p-part of Sha.

requests.need: The integral inverse determinant Δ_p(T) = det⁻¹ RΓ_c(O_{K,S_p}, T) of a Galois-stable lattice, with its rationalization, derived base change and triangle isomorphisms, and the Selmer local determinant formula det⁻¹ C_f ≅ det⁻¹ C_c ⊗ ⊗_v det⁻¹ U_v^+, both as constructions that use only ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7, SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 and the determinant functor: the prerequisite PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.0 is to be removed from M.8/arithmetic-fundamental-line and M.8/selmer-local-determinant-comparison, whose rational fundamental line, real and p-adic comparisons and Tamagawa clause are planned here (FL.2–FL.4). The Deligne–Borel lattice half of M.8/regulator-determinant-comparison stays in M.8 for M.8/number-field-chern-lattice-index.

realTrivialization (PS.3.2), the rational line Ξ_A(M) (PS.3.1) and LeadingTermRational (PS.3.3) stated for supplied motivic factors and exact-sequence witnesses, with no import of MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/arithmetic-fundamental-line or M.8/regulator-determinant-comparison; the Tate and elliptic instances are the theorems FL.2/real-exactness-artin, FL.2/real-exactness-elliptic and FL.2/fundamental-line-real-comparison here.

The λ-adic lattice I_λ(M, T, S) of PS.4.1 with the rational comparison θ_λ as a hypothesis (as stated there), the local Euler and Tamagawa identifications of PS.4.3 and the real dyadic restriction of PS.4.4, importing from MotivicEtaleKTheory only Δ_λ(T) and none of the fundamental-line comparisons planned here.

The graded determinant functor on perfect complexes over commutative rings: multiplicativity on true triangles, derived base change, shift inversion, the Koszul sign of swapping odd factors, and the acyclic trivialization distinguished from the identity trivialization of [V → V].
Mordell–Weil over the number field K and the canonical (Néron–Tate) height pairing, positive definite on E(K) ⊗ ℝ, with its regulator.
The Abel–Jacobi isomorphism Pic⁰(E) ≅ E(K), P ↦ [P] − [O].
The Weil pairing on Tate modules, giving h¹(E)^∨ ≅ h¹(E)(1) on realizations.
Selmer groups and Sha of E over K with the Kummer exact sequence, to compare finiteness of Sha[p^∞] with surjectivity of the Kummer realization.
Hodge decomposition, Hodge symmetry and strictness for the Hodge structures H^i(σX(ℂ)), used for the weight argument and the Deligne cohomology identification.

remaining: Noncommutative coefficient algebras: A-equivariance of the integral images is stated through correspondences; projectivity of the factors over orders is not planned here (Burns–Flach coherence hypothesis).
The weight −1 height pairing for motives other than h¹ of elliptic curves is a datum (gap G1).
Inclusion of the p-adic realization of the integral part in H¹_f outside the listed cases is a hypothesis (gap G3).

Functional-equation compatibility of the condition between M and M*(1) in general twists (Huber–Kings Proposition 2.2.3) is used only in the class number formula case; its general statement needs the local epsilon isomorphisms of NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.7.

gaps.title: G1: Beilinson–Bloch height pairing in weight −1
gaps.detail: The map δ of the Beilinson regulator sequence in weight −1 is the Néron–Tate pairing for h¹(E)(1) (TauCetiRoadmap EllipticCurves Layer 6), but for general M = h^{2j−1}(X)(j) it is the archimedean-plus-nonarchimedean Beilinson–Bloch height on CH^j(X)_{hom∼0} (Fontaine §9.6, p. 233). No roadmap constructs it: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.7/height-positivity-predicate takes it as a datum. Here it is a datum of the sequence outside the elliptic case.

gaps.title: G2: Independence of the integral part of the regular model
gaps.detail: H¹_f(K, M) is defined from a recorded regular proper model 𝒳 (as in MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8/integral-motivic-structures). Its independence of 𝒳, and its definition when no regular model exists (Scholl's construction via alterations, cited by Burns–Flach p. 518 as [41]), are not planned by any roadmap; they are not needed for Artin motives (the model Spec O_F is canonical) or for elliptic curves with a chosen regular model.

gaps.title: G3: The p-adic realization of the integral part lies in H¹_f
gaps.detail: MotivicEtaleKTheory and PadicHodgeRegulators give the syntomic factorization and the inclusion in H¹_g (Nekovář–Nizioł); equality with H¹_f holds locally in weights ≤ −3 at good reduction, for Artin motives of positive twist and for h¹(E)(1). At bad primes and in weights −1, −2 outside these cases the inclusion in H¹_f (Fontaine §9.4, p. 232, conjectural in general, Gros under hypotheses) is a hypothesis; no roadmap plans the general statement.
